_comment: Speech-to-speech / realtime model pricing for the mivas-bench S2S harnesses. Use with the gen_ai.usage.* token counts the report.py tracers emit to estimate LLM cost per call. `null` = the model has no such lane.

units.audio_rates: tokens per second of audio, or USD per minute of audio, as published by the provider

normalize_model_id: lowercase, strip provider prefix before the last '/', strip @YYYYMMDD and -YYYY-MM-DD date suffixes, collapse -preview-MM-YYYY to -preview, and -native-audio-preview to -native-audio

token_pricing._note_gpt-live-1-backends: Backend Responses models behind openai/gpt-live-1 (sol-low, astra-medium), text only. Standard tier from https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, checked 2026-09-26. The live voice session is billed on top per minute (per_minute_pricing gpt-live-1).
token_pricing._note_gemini-3.8-live: Live API pricing page 2026-09-26: same rates as 3.1 flash live; output price includes thinking tokens, so the extended-thinking variant bills its reasoning as output.
token_pricing._note_gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview: Unused, and this id no longer appears on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (checked 2026-08-22). Vertex still lists a 'Gemini 2.5 Flash Live API' row at 0.50 / 3.00 / 2.00 / 12.00 — the rates below are stale. Do not price against this row.
token_pricing._note_qwen-omni-output-audio: outputAudio for the two rows below was read off the 文本（多模态输入）column, ~5x low; corrected 2026-08-22 from the 文本+音频（仅音频计费）column on https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/model-pricing (Singapore/international CNY ÷ 7.34).
token_pricing._note_qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus: NO LONGER A PROXY (corrected 2026-08-22). The id is absent from the English pricing page but IS listed on https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/model-pricing — Singapore/国际 row 5.995 / 47.963 / 47.963 / 179.861 CNY per 1M tokens, ÷ 7.4938 (the rate Alibaba itself implies where both currencies are printed) = 0.80 / 6.40 / 6.40 / 24.00 USD. The old rates were proxied from qwen3.5-omni-plus-realtime and ran ~2.6x too high. Realtime usage carries no cached_tokens lane.
token_pricing._note_gpt-4.1: Text-only LLM leg of the livekit/cascaded pair (Deepgram Flux + gpt-4.1 + ElevenLabs Flash v2.5); see component_pricing for the other two legs. Verified 2026-08-22 on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.

_note_verified: Every row in active benchmark use was re-verified against the vendor's official page on 2026-09-29: gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-live-1 on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing plus the model pages; gemini-3.8-live, gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking, gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview and gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing; amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0 on the AWS Price List API offer file https://pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/AmazonBedrock/current/us-east-1/index.csv (publication 2026-09-01, USE1-NovaSonic2.0-* SKUs, per-1K x 1000; the aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing table is script-rendered and the old b0.p.awsstatic.com map is gone); qwen-audio-3.0-realtime-plus on https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing (Singapore / International, now printed in USD: 0.80 / 6.40 / 6.40 / 24.00); grok-voice-latest on https://docs.x.ai/docs/models; Deepgram Flux on https://deepgram.com/pricing; ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 on https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api. Only the ElevenLabs rate changed (component_pricing.tts). Earlier check: 2026-08-22.
_note_cached_semantics: cachedText/cachedAudio are the DISCOUNTED rate for tokens that are already inside the input lane, not an extra lane. Bill (input - cached) at the input rate + cached at the cached rate. Confirmed for OpenAI (input_token_details.cached_tokens sits inside input_tokens) and Gemini (promptTokenCount 'includes the number of tokens in the cached content'). Bedrock is the exception — it reports cacheReadInputTokens ALONGSIDE inputTokens — but neither Nova Sonic id supports prompt caching, so no cached tokens ever appear.
_note_gemini_undercount: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-29: eval_costs now reads usage from the realtime_inference span and its child realtime_metrics span (livekit-agents 1.8 layout) as well as from agent_turn, and any generation that still carries no packet (about 1% of Gemini 3.8 agent_turns, almost all the final farewell turn whose socket closes before turn_complete) is priced from its measured speech seconds and transcript at the published audio_rates below. No factor is applied anywhere. Historical note follows. Gemini traces show ~40% of agent_turn spans with no gen_ai.usage.*, but MOST of those are not missing tokens. Verified on the wire (LK_GOOGLE_DEBUG frame capture, run 254007, 3.1 legal): Gemini sends ONE usage_metadata per server turn, at turn_complete, and it AGGREGATES every model invocation in that turn — a turn with a tool call bills ~2x the per-invocation prompt, a turn with two bills ~3x. livekit opens a separate _ResponseGeneration (hence a separate agent_turn span) for each invocation, so spans outnumber usage packets ~2:1. The plugin drops nothing: 22 generations, 9 usage packets, 9 turn_completes, zero 'no active generation' warnings. The only REAL loss is a turn whose socket we close before turn_complete — the handoff transfer call at the end of each stage, plus the final end_call turn — 4 such turns on that call, each one invocation. Sized from the per-invocation prompt of the neighbouring reported turn: 18,770 of 93,816 input tokens, i.e. a correction of x1.25, not x1.5. Unfixable client-side without letting the old stage reply after the transfer (permanent-mute risk); the possible upstream route is livekit-plugins-google >=1.7.0 NON_BLOCKING tools with silent scheduling, untested. The CSVs are NOT inflated by this factor — apply ~x1.25 when quoting gemini cost.
_note_grok_text_input: xAI's price sheet lists '$0.004 / text input' under Speech to Speech beside the $0.08 audio minute (https://docs.x.ai/docs/models, 2026-09-29). The only text the grok harness injects into a live conversation is one conversation.item.create (function_call_output) per tool call, so eval_costs bills one text input per execute_tool span at per_text_input_pricing. xAI does not define 'text input' any further; whether tool results count is the open question, so the line is kept separate in llm_cost_detail.

per_text_input_pricing._note_: USD per text input item, xAI Speech to Speech line item (see _note_grok_text_input).

audio_rates._note_: Provider-published conversions used ONLY for generations that never received a usage packet (llm_cost_source carries +backfill and llm_cost_backfilled_turns counts them). *TokensPerSecond entries convert measured speech seconds into tokens billed at token_pricing; *UsdPerMinute entries are the provider's own per-minute audio price and are applied directly. textCharsPerToken is the provider's documented approximation for transcript / tool-call text.
audio_rates._note_openai: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/voice-latency-cost 2026-09-29: 'Audio tokens in user messages are 1 token per 100 ms of audio, while audio tokens in assistant messages are 1 token per 50ms of audio.' Same guide: earlier-turn content is cached best-effort, so backfilled turns bill everything before the newest user message at cachedText/cachedAudio. Text ~4 chars per token per OpenAI's tokenizer guide.
audio_rates._note_gemini: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing 2026-09-29, Gemini 3.8 Live / 3.1 Flash Live row: input '$3.00 or $0.005/min (audio)', output '$12.00 or $0.018/min (audio)' — the per-minute prices are applied directly to measured seconds ($0.018/min at $12/1M implies 25 tokens/s, which is what the 3.8 usage packets show empirically: ~26 tok/s). https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/tokens: 'Audio: 32 tokens per second', 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'. The 2.5 native-audio row publishes no per-minute figure, so it uses 32 tokens/s at its token rates.
audio_rates._note_qwen: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing 2026-09-29, Real-time Voice Chat billing: 'Total tokens = Audio duration (seconds) x 12.5. Durations less than 1 second are rounded up to 1 second.' Alibaba's rules: user audio stays in context as audio input every later turn, model output audio is billed once and not re-sent, instructions and output text are billed as text.
audio_rates._note_nova: AWS publishes no audio-seconds-to-token conversion for Nova Sonic (usage arrives only as usageEvent, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/output-events.html); no backfill rule exists and every scored Nova row carries usage packets.
audio_rates._note_gpt-live-1: gpt-live-1 backend turns with no chat span are reconstructed as gpt-6-astra / gpt-5.6-sol Responses calls: prompt + accumulated transcript at textCharsPerToken 4, prior context at the cached rate; the voice leg is per-minute and needs no token conversion.

per_minute_pricing._note_: grok-voice-latest is an alias of grok-voice-think-fast-2.0 (verified 2026-08-22, https://docs.x.ai/docs/models: '$0.08 / min ($4.80 / hr) audio'). xAI meters the speech-to-speech model as ONE per-minute charge, not as separate STT/LLM/TTS legs — grok-stt ($0.10/hr REST, $0.20/hr streaming) and grok-tts ($15.00/1M chars) are separate products that a cascaded pipeline would pay for instead. Duration minutes are the right billing basis. Add $0.01/min if xAI PSTN telephony is used (we use CHIRP, so no).
per_minute_pricing._note_gpt-live-1: GPT-Live meters the voice session per minute, billed per second with no rounding ($0.05/min, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing and /models/gpt-live-1, checked 2026-09-29). eval_costs bills the API-reported mivas.live.usage_seconds from the voice.call span when present, else duration_s. The backend Responses model is billed separately on its own tokens — price those from the chat spans, not from this row.

component_pricing._comment: Non-LLM legs of the livekit/cascaded pair, priced from the mivas.stt.audio_duration_s / mivas.tts.characters attrs on the voice.call root. cost_usd = cost_llm_usd + cost_stt_usd + cost_tts_usd.

stt.unit: USD per minute of streamed audio
stt._note_: https://deepgram.com/pricing 2026-09-29 (unchanged since 2026-08-22): Flux English streaming pay-as-you-go shows 'Current price $0.0065/min' under a 'Limited-time promotional rates on streaming' banner, 'Regular price $0.0077/min'. The regular rate is used so the benchmark is not pegged to a promo. (Nova-3 monolingual streaming is the same $0.0077/min regular.)

tts._note_: https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api 2026-09-29: ElevenLabs now publishes USD API rates — 'Flash / Turbo: $0.04 per 1K characters' (FAQ: 'Text to Speech: $0.08 per 1,000 characters (multilingual models) or $0.04 (Flash/Turbo)'). Replaces the $0.0825 that was derived on 2026-08-22 from subscription credits (0.5 credits/char at the Pro/Business $0.000165/credit), which overstated the TTS leg ~2x.
